detail.body:
### What does this PR do?

Closes #1524.

Clarify the units and arithmetic behind GRPO/PPO train, mini and micro batch sizes. The configured actor and critic `ppo_mini_batch_size` values are prompt-equivalent global sizes; the trainers multiply them by `rollout.n` before partitioning trajectories across the corresponding data-parallel ranks.

Add the issue's `1024 / 256 / 80 / n=5` worked example, formulas for fixed-size gradient accumulation and optimizer-update counts, and explicit boundaries for dynamic token-budget batching, forward-only log-probability batches, multi-output rollouts, filtering, padding and asynchronous replay.

The explanation is linked from the PPO guide, configuration reference and batch-size FAQ. This changes documentation only: no runtime behavior, defaults, APIs, dependencies or CI configuration change.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs. Queries: [#1524 references](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+1524+in%3Abody), [batch-size documentation](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+%22batch+size%22+documentation), and [GRPO batch](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+GRPO+batch). No direct implementation was found. Related open PRs #8201, #6025 and #8026 concern mini-batch balancing, multi-output trajectories and batch invariance respectively; their relevant file diffs were inspected and they do not provide this worked unit explanation.
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`.

### Test

The human submitter reviewed every changed line and confirmed completing the relevant local testing before submission, as required by `AGENTS.md`.

Automated checks run locally on Linux with Python 3.12.3:

- `pre-commit run --all-files --show-diff-on-failure --color=never`: all 14 hooks passed.
- `python -m pytest tests/special_sanity/test_config_docs.py tests/special_sanity/test_check_example_naming.py -q`: 15 passed.
- `git diff --check main`: passed.
- Full Sphinx HTML build completed. The generated example anchor, table and all three cross-page links were inspected programmatically and resolve correctly.
- A local-only verifier independently parsed the documented YAML and confirmed the expected counts: 5,120 rollout trajectories, 1,280 trajectories per global actor mini-batch, 160 per actor DP rank, two micro-batches per optimizer update, four updates for one PPO epoch and eight for two epochs.

The full Sphinx build reports 328 warnings on both the patch and untouched `main` in the same isolated documentation environment. After normalizing checkout paths and shifted source line numbers, the warning content is identical: zero diagnostic lines were added or removed. These include existing duplicate section labels, existing references/highlighting warnings and API autodoc imports unavailable in the isolated docs dependency set; this is not claimed as a warning-free build.

No model downloads, provider calls, GPU/multiprocess training, end-to-end training, complete training dependency installation, or non-Linux platform testing were performed. Those are not needed to exercise this documentation-only change.

### API and Usage Example

No API or configuration behavior changes. The documentation now explains the existing calculation. For the issue's fixed-size example with eight actor data-parallel ranks:

```text
B=1024, n=5, M=256, d=8, m=80, E=1
rollout trajectories = B*n = 5120
global actor mini-batch = M*n = 1280
local actor mini-batch = M*n/d = 160
micro-batches per optimizer update = M*n/(d*m) = 2
actor optimizer updates = (B/M)*E = 4
```

### Design & Code Changes

- Correct the canonical `actor_rollout_ref.rollout.n` key and explain that configured PPO mini-batches use prompt-equivalent global units.
- Add a symbol table, formulas, divisibility checks and the original worked example to the GRPO guide.
- Distinguish actor data-parallel size from rollout tensor parallelism or total GPU count.
- Explain that dynamic token-budget micro-batching does not have a fixed micro-batch count and that rollout/reference log-probability micro-batches are forward-only.
- Cross-link the shared explanation from PPO, the configuration reference and FAQ.

AI assistance from OpenAI Codex was used for issue auditing, documentation drafting and validation. The human submitter reviewed every changed line, ran the relevant tests, understands the calculation and remains responsible for the contribution.

### Checklist Before Submitting

- [x] Read the [Contribute Guide](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] Apply [pre-commit checks](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#code-linting-and-formatting): all 14 hooks passed.
- [x] Add / Update [the documentation](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/tree/main/docs).
- [x] Add unit or end-to-end test(s) to the CI workflow, or explain why tests are not applicable: no new runtime behavior exists; existing documentation/config sanity tests and the Sphinx build cover the changed files.
- [ ] Once the PR is ready for CI, send a message in the `ci-request` Slack channel or Feishu group. I do not have access to either channel from this environment, so this has not been represented as completed.
- [x] If related to the `recipe` submodule, update its reference. Not applicable; the submodule is unchanged.

+(grpo-batch-size-example)=
+### Batch sizes and optimizer updates
+
+The following counts apply to a complete synchronous rollout batch in which each sampled response produces one training trajectory, with actor updates enabled. They do not describe extra trajectories emitted by custom multi-output agent loops, dynamic filtering, synthetic padding, or asynchronous replay-buffer sampling.
+
+| Symbol | Setting or quantity | Unit |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `B` | `data.train_batch_size` | Prompts in one global rollout batch |
+| `n` | `actor_rollout_ref.rollout.n` | Responses sampled per prompt |
+| `M` | `actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_mini_batch_size` | Global prompt-equivalent mini-batch size, expanded to `M * n` trajectories |
+| `d` | Actor data-parallel size | Ranks that partition the actor training batch |
+| `m` | `actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_micro_batch_size_per_gpu` | Trajectories per local forward/backward pass when `use_dynamic_bsz=False` |
+| `E` | `actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_epochs` | Passes over the sampled training batch |
+
+Both PPO trainers expand `M` by `n` before calling the actor update. The worker then divides that trajectory count by the actor engine's data-parallel size. "Prompt-equivalent" describes the configured size; it does not guarantee that all responses to a prompt stay together after shuffling or batch balancing.
+
+For evenly divisible fixed-size batches:
+
+```text
+trajectories per rollout batch          = B * n
+trajectories per global actor mini-batch = M * n
+trajectories per local actor mini-batch  = M * n / d
+micro-batches per optimizer update      = M * n / (d * m)
+actor optimizer updates per rollout batch = (B / M) * E
+```
+
+Use the **actor** data-parallel size for `d`, not the rollout tensor-parallel size or the total number of GPUs unless all actor GPUs are data-parallel ranks. For example, actor tensor, pipeline, or sequence parallelism can make `d` smaller than the total actor GPU count.
+
+#### Worked example
+
+Consider these settings with 8 actor data-parallel ranks and fixed micro-batching:
+
+```yaml
+data.train_batch_size: 1024
+actor_rollout_ref.rollout.n: 5
+actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_mini_batch_size: 256
+actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_micro_batch_size_per_gpu: 80
+actor_rollout_ref.actor.use_dynamic_bsz: false
+actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_epochs: 1
+```
+
+One rollout batch samples `1024 * 5 = 5120` trajectories. Each global actor mini-batch contains `256 * 5 = 1280` trajectories, so each actor DP rank receives `1280 / 8 = 160` trajectories per optimizer update. Each rank processes two micro-batches of 80 trajectories and accumulates their gradients before the optimizer step.
+
+Thus, `80` does **not** need to divide the configured `256`; it needs to divide the local expanded mini-batch size `160`. The rollout batch produces `1024 / 256 = 4` actor optimizer updates with `ppo_epochs=1`, or 8 updates with `ppo_epochs=2`. A trainer step consumes the rollout batch; it is not necessarily a single optimizer update. Increasing `ppo_epochs` reuses the sampled trajectories rather than generating another `B * n` responses for each epoch.
+
+For this fixed-size case, check that `B` is divisible by `M`, `M * n` is divisible by `d`, and `M * n / d` is divisible by `m`. These are batch-count constraints, not a guarantee that the configuration fits in GPU memory.
+
+#### Dynamic and forward-only micro-batches
+
+With `actor_rollout_ref.actor.use_dynamic_bsz=True`, micro-batches are formed using the token budget `actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_max_token_len_per_gpu` and sequence lengths instead of the fixed trajectory count `m`. The fixed-size accumulation formula above no longer predicts the number of micro-batches. The global rollout and mini-batch counts remain the same under the stated assumptions.
+
+`actor_rollout_ref.rollout.log_prob_micro_batch_size_per_gpu` and `actor_rollout_ref.ref.log_prob_micro_batch_size_per_gpu` control local **forward-only** batches for actor and reference log-probability evaluation. They do not set the actor optimizer mini-batch size or its gradient-accumulation count. Their corresponding `log_prob_use_dynamic_bsz` and `log_prob_max_token_len_per_gpu` settings select token-budget batching instead when enabled.
+

# Contributor License Agreement (CLA) assistant

Streamline your workflow and let CLA assistant handle the legal side of contributions to a repository for you. CLA assistant enables contributors to sign CLAs from within a pull request.

To get started, simply store your CLA as a GitHub Gist file then link it with the repository/organisation in CLA assistant. Then sit back and relax while CLA assistant:

- Comments on each opened pull request to ask the contributor to sign the CLA
- Allows contributors to sign a CLA from within a pull request
- Authenticates the signee with their GitHub account
- Updates the status of a pull request when the contributor agrees to the CLA
- Automatically asks users to re-sign the CLA for each new pull request in the event the associated Gist & CLA has changed
- Green lights merge queues without additional CLA checks as everyone needs to have signed of on the PR level already

Repository owners can review a list of users who signed the CLA for each version of it. To get started, visit [cla-assistant.io](https://cla-assistant.io).
